A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BD-LoRA research and contain 65 readable pages, including Appendices A–F. Full-document text and rendering comparisons support a reliable comparison; the appendices are unchanged.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments on GLUE and OpenOrca and serving latency and throughput experiments in Section 5 and Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original fine-tuning and serving experiments, including their numerical tables and plots.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same block-diagonal constraints, sharding procedures, adapter training and scaling. The new mention of slightly updated public code does not describe a methodological revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight GLUE tasks, OpenOrca and serving scenarios, including cached and distinct adapters and quantized base models. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain standard LoRA for fine-tuning comparisons and S-LoRA and NFS-LoRA for runtime comparisons, including the appendix experiments.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain the same models, hyperparameters, data quantities, metrics, hardware and batch/token settings, including the 128-request runtime protocol. No revised evaluation procedure is reported.

E4.justification: The adapter-placement and scaling comparisons in Appendix E and the TP-degree, adapter-loading and hardware analyses in Appendix F are unchanged. No ablation or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same ten-, five- and three-run fine-tuning configurations, confidence intervals and runtime variability reporting. Neither run counts nor uncertainty-reporting practices change.

E6.justification: The empirical tables, plotted results and reported findings are unchanged throughout. For example, Table 28 retains BD-LoRA's reported E2E speedups of 1.26x over S-LoRA and 1.17x over NFS-LoRA.

T1.justification: The block-diagonal mathematical formulation in Section 3 and the compute and memory derivations in Appendix A, including Table 1, are unchanged. No mathematical result or proof is added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same claims: eliminating additional LoRA communication, preserving comparable downstream performance at similar parameter counts and improving serving speed.

C2.justification: The explanations of decoding speedups and overlapping confidence intervals remain unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations of knowing the TP degree during training and needing to train BD-LoRA adapters from scratch.

D1.justification: Section 1 replaces the intention to merge code into vLLM with a link to a draft serving-code pull request and reports training code merged into Hugging Face PEFT, with an access link. This improves resource-access information; Appendix C's implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited research and positioning relative to S-LoRA, Punica, communication-overlap approaches and other adaptation methods are unchanged. The new code links provide implementation access rather than new research comparisons.

P1.justification: v2 revises the code-availability paragraph, extends the acknowledgment to credit code upgrading and open-sourcing, and removes a duplicated 'with' in Section 6. The section organization and scientific narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 moves from page 3 to page 4 without changing its diagram or caption. The code announcement receives bold emphasis and nearby text reflows; no figures or tables are added, removed or substantively redesigned.

improvement.justification: v2 replaces a future code-release intention with concrete access information for serving and training implementations, improving reproducibility documentation and practical reuse. The scientific content and supporting evidence remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
